S53.01.note: How Settings opens from the sidebar was not confirmed in the code; the Settings > Skills path is taken from the settings navigation.
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and click Skills under Customize.
Click Browse at the top right of the Skills list.
Scroll the catalogue and look for skills that are not installed yet.
Click a skill name and check that its detail page opens, with an Install button if it is not installed.
Compare with Expected: you can browse uninstalled skills and open any of them.

S53.02.note: The manage list is built from the directory adapter; the exact row layout was not rendered in the code read.
steps: Open Settings and click Skills under Customize.
Look at the list: each row shows the skill name, its Author (You, AGI or Managed), Last updated, and a status.
Compare with Expected: the list shows the skills installed or active for this account.

S53.03.needs: a signed-in account that can create skills
S53.03.note: The Create action only appears when the account can author skills (onCreateSkill is capability-gated); the empty state says No skills of your own yet.
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, then click Add.
Click Create a skill.
Type a Name, a Description and Instructions, then click Create skill.
Look in the Skills list for the new skill with Author shown as You.
Compare with Expected: the skill belongs only to this account and appears as personal.
S53.03.where: Settings > Skills > Add > Create a skill

steps: Open Settings, click Skills.
Click any skill name in the list.
Check that the detail page shows the description, the Source and access section, and a Skill files list.
Click a file in Skill files and check that its contents show below.
Compare with Expected: description, instructions and files are visible.
S53.06.where: Settings > Skills > click a skill name

S53.07.note: The row description is set by the directory adapter; the exact row text was not checked against a rendered screen.
steps: Open Settings, click Skills.
Read the name and any description shown on each row.
Click a skill and check the Description field in the detail page.
Compare with Expected: each skill shows its name and what it does.

S53.08.note: The line Use one in chat with / or @ is in the fallback SkillsPanel in SettingsModal.tsx; the code read did not confirm the web app shows it.
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open an installed skill.
Click Try in chat; the chat opens with that skill selected.
Or in the chat box, type / and look for the Skills group listing skill names.
Compare with Expected: the product shows how a skill is started (slash name, button or automatic matching).
S53.08.where: Settings > Skills > open an installed skill > Try in chat; or type / in the chat box

S53.09.needs: a personal skill you can edit
S53.09.note: The edit control's exact label on the row was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, click Add, then Create a skill.
Find the Instructions field and type some text.
Click Create skill and check the new skill appears in the list.
Reopen an editable skill and change Instructions, then click Save changes.
Compare with Expected: the instructions can be written and edited in the product.
S53.09.where: Settings > Skills > Add > Create a skill (or open an existing skill and click its edit control)

S53.10.note: Only the viewing of bundled files is reachable from UI; reading them during a run is not visible from the UI.
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open a skill that has more than one file.
Look at the Skill files list on the left.
Click a non-SKILL.md file and check that its contents appear.
Compare with Expected: the skill's bundled reference files are visible. Whether the model reads them during a run is server-side and not checked here.
S53.10.where: Settings > Skills > open a skill > Skill files

S53.11.needs: a skill with a script bundle
S53.11.note: Script execution is in apps/web/lib/e2b/skill-staging.ts and the tool loop; the UI only shows the files.
steps: Open a skill that bundles a script file in Settings > Skills.
Check that the script file appears in Skill files.
Use the skill in chat and see whether the reply reflects the script's output.
S53.11.where: Skill files list in a skill's detail page (script files appear there); runs happen server-side

S53.14.needs: a skill that declares required tools
S53.14.note: The row only shows the requirement; enforcement is in the server skill route, which the code read did not run.
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open a skill.
Look under Source and access for the Needs tools row.
Compare with Expected: the tools the skill needs are listed as names.
S53.14.where: Settings > Skills > open a skill > Source and access > Needs tools

S53.15.needs: a skill that declares required connectors; an outside account if the connector needs sign-in
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open a skill that needs a connector.
Look under Source and access at Needs connectors.
Check each connector shows Connected, Not connected, or a Connect button.
Click Connect if shown and check the state changes.
Compare with Expected: the required connections are shown.
S53.15.where: Settings > Skills > open a skill > Source and access > Needs connectors

S53.17.needs: an installed skill; a model that supports tools
S53.17.note: The + label is a translation default value; the reply's use of the skill is checked by the server.
steps: Open a chat and click the + button labelled Add attachments and tools.
Click Skills and pick a skill from the list.
Type a message and send it.
Compare with Expected: the reply follows that skill's instructions.
S53.17.where: Chat box > Add attachments and tools (+) > Skills > pick a skill; or type / in the chat box

S53.18.needs: an installed skill; a model that supports tools
S53.18.note: The offer is applied server-side in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts (applyImplicitManagedSkillOffer) and skips some surfaces and any request with a tool choice.
steps: Install a skill with a clear description, then in a new chat send a message that matches that description without choosing a skill.
Check whether the reply follows that skill's instructions.
S53.18.where: No control; the chat reply uses a matching skill without a pick

S53.20.note: The switch is not shown for skills you created (editable skills get Delete instead), so personal skills can only be deleted, not switched off.
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, then click the skill (or Browse for a catalogue skill).
Turn off the Enable skill switch.
Check the skill stays in the list but no longer appears in the / menu in chat.
Turn the switch on again and check it comes back.
Compare with Expected: the skill is turned off and on without being deleted.
S53.20.where: Settings > Skills > Browse > open an installed skill > Enable skill

S53.21.needs: a file to upload (a .zip with SKILL.md inside, a .skill file, or a SKILL.md)
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, click Add, then Upload a skill.
Choose a .zip, .skill or SKILL.md file from your computer and click Upload.
Check the skill appears in the Skills list.
Use it in chat with / and check the reply follows it.
Compare with Expected: the uploaded skill can be used.
S53.21.where: Settings > Skills > Add > Upload a skill; or Settings > Skills > Add > Create a skill > Import a SKILL.md

S53.22.note: Download is per file; no whole-skill export was found in the code read.
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open a skill.
Click a file in Skill files.
Click Download file.
Check that the file saves to your computer with its contents.
Compare with Expected: the skill's files can be downloaded.
S53.22.where: Settings > Skills > open a skill > click a file in Skill files > Download file

steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open a skill.
Read the Source and access section.
Check the Source, Added, Version, Needs tools, Needs connectors and Access rows.
Compare with Expected: the skill's permissions and where it came from are summarised.
S53.36.where: Settings > Skills > open a skill > Source and access
